about: Tasks to try the skill on. Each is one line, as a person would ask it, given to an agent that has this skill and a project with the packages named in `project`. `expect` and `reject` are what to look for in the files it writes: each is a regular expression, and a short reason. See README.md beside this file.

evals.prompt: Add a form to invite a teammate: their name, their email, a role picked from Admin, Member and Viewer, and a Send invite button. Show an error under a field that's wrong.

expect.why: The components are imported from the package, and not written again.
Each control is in a Field.
Each control has a label that's tied to it.
The control is inside FieldControl, which is what ties them.
The error is a FieldError, read with its control.
A Button is type="button" unless told otherwise.
A control without a name isn't in the form's data.

reject.why: A color written out. Every color is a token.
Tailwind color utilities in place of the theme's tokens.
A label written by hand for a control that's in a Field. Field makes the ids, and FieldLabel is the label.
There's no folder of copied components. They're installed.

evals.prompt: Add a Delete project button that asks for confirmation before it deletes.

expect.why: A confirmation is a dialog, and one that destroys something is an AlertDialog.
The title is the dialog's name. Without one a screen reader has nothing to say.
The trigger takes the Button through asChild, and isn't a button around a button.
The button that deletes says so by its intent.

reject.why: The browser's own box, which can't be themed and reads badly.
A prop that doesn't exist. The title is a part.

evals.prompt: Show a list of orders in a table that can be sorted by date and by total: order number, customer, date, total.

expect.why: Tables are in their own package.
A table that sorts is a DataTable, made with the hook.
The file that calls the hook is a client component.
A data table needs a name.

reject.why: A table written by hand, in place of the library's.
Sorting written by hand, in place of the table's own.

evals.prompt: Make the app use our brand color, a dark green, for primary buttons and links, and follow the visitor's system for dark mode.

expect.why: The brand's color is the primary token, set in CSS.
Dark mode is an attribute on the page.

reject.why: Never needed: a rule outside the layers already wins.
There's no provider and no theme object. Theming is CSS.
The component restyled by its class, where a token or a variable does it.

evals.prompt: When the settings form is saved, tell the user it worked.

expect.why: A message that passes is a toast.
Something has to show it. Rendered once, near the root, if it isn't there yet.

evals.prompt: Add a bar chart of revenue by month for this year and last year.

expect.why: A chart goes in the container, which sizes it and sets its colors.
The container needs the series described.
A chart needs a name.
A series takes its color from the container's variables, so it follows the theme.
A chart is a client component.

evals.prompt: Show our three offices on a map, each with its address when it's pressed.

expect.why: Without the worker's address the map never loads.
The map has no tiles of its own.
A place is a marker.
A marker is read by its name.
The map says what it's of.

reject.why: MapLibre's stylesheet isn't loaded. The package's own has what's needed.

evals.ask: Which tile provider to use. It's the owner's choice, with terms and a cost, and an agent that picks one without asking has got this wrong.

evals.prompt: Put a small button with a trash icon at the end of each row to delete it.

expect.why: It's a Button.
A button with only an icon has no name unless it's given one.

reject.why: A div that's pressed can't be reached or worked by keyboard.
